name: American Tower
description: American Tower owns about 131,600 towers (and operates about 17,200 more it does not own) in more than 20 countries and rents space on them to wireless carriers, broadcasters and government users. The tenant pays: carriers sign long master leases with annual rent escalators and add equipment to existing towers, so each added tenant on an existing tower is close to pure profit. Only about 49 percent of revenue comes from the US and Canada; the rest is Africa and Asia-Pacific, Europe and Latin America, where power and fuel costs are partly passed through. It also owns CoreSite data centers (about 10 percent of revenue). Three carriers (T-Mobile 18%, AT&T 17%, Verizon 14% of total 2025 revenue) plus Telefonica (10%) dominate the tenant base. The India business (ATC TIPL) is reported as discontinued.

businessLines.name: U.S. & Canada property
businessLines.how: Leases space on towers and rooftops to the big three US carriers (AT&T, T-Mobile, Verizon Wireless were 85% of segment revenue); rent is paid monthly under long master leases with annual escalators plus fees when carriers add equipment.

businessLines.name: Africa & APAC property
businessLines.how: Tower rent from mobile operators (Airtel and MTN are the top tenants); part is pass-through of power and fuel costs, so revenue includes cost recovery.

operatingProfit.label: Segment operating profit (gross margin less segment SG&A)

businessLines.name: Europe property
businessLines.how: Tower rent from European operators under long contracts, mostly Germany, Spain and France.

operatingProfit.label: Segment operating profit (gross margin less segment SG&A)

businessLines.name: Latin America property
businessLines.how: Tower rent from Latin American operators (Brazil has the most towers), billed in local currencies so FX moves reported revenue.

operatingProfit.label: Segment operating profit (gross margin less segment SG&A)

businessLines.name: Data Centers
businessLines.how: CoreSite colocation and interconnection: customers pay monthly for space and power and for cross-connects in US data centers.

operatingProfit.label: Segment operating profit (gross margin less segment SG&A)

businessLines.name: Services
businessLines.how: One-time fees for site application, zoning, structural analysis and construction work that supports adding tenants to towers.
